title: Optimal Quantum-Circuit Synthesis and Implementation of General Unitaries with Parallelized Bitstring-Conditioned Rotations
authors: Heikki Suominen, Suman Kundu, Heidi Kivijärvi, Sasu Tuohino, Mikko Tuokkola, Eemeli Forsbom, Madhavi Chand, Vasilii Vadimov, R. Vijay, Mikko Möttönen
abstract: We theoretically introduce a quantum-circuit synthesis protocol to realize any $n$-qubit transformation $U\in U(2^n)$, up to a diagonal. The resulting circuit is directly native to and optimal in gate count and depth for systems where bitstring-conditioned rotations with tunable angle and axis, $C^{(n-1)}R(θ,φ)$, form the set of native operations. Subsequently, we suggest how this protocol can be implemented in a few-mode superconducting circuit, and experimentally demonstrate the method for the smallest nontrivial case, i.e., for two qubits. We report an average gate fidelity of 97.6 % for Haar-random two-qubit unitaries up to phase shifts in the computational basis. Importantly, these results suggest that multimode devices, such as those in the multimon or multiunimon families may become competitive with qubit-array networks for general-unitary implementations for qubit counts as low as three.
summary: This paper introduces an optimal quantum-circuit synthesis protocol to implement any $n$-qubit unitary using only bitstring-conditioned rotations native to certain superconducting hardware. The authors prove the circuit depth is minimal and experimentally validate the method on two qubits, suggesting that multimode superconducting devices are highly competitive for general quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of developing an optimal quantum-circuit synthesis protocol to realize any general $n$-qubit unitary transformation $U \in U(2^n)$ using a restricted set of native gates.
main_result: They achieve a circuit depth of $2^{n-1}$ for the effective unitary, which is proven to be optimal based on parameter counting, and demonstrated a gate fidelity of 97.6% for two-qubit random unitaries.
method: The protocol modifies quantum-circuit synthesis using the Cosine-Sine Decomposition (CSD) to transpile the target unitary into a sequence of bitstring-conditioned rotations, $C^{(n-1)}R(	heta, \phi)$.
model_or_system: The work is theoretically developed for general $n$-qubit systems but is experimentally demonstrated using a few-mode superconducting circuit, specifically referencing superconducting trimon or multiunimon architectures.
key_observables: Average gate fidelity (97.6% for 2 qubits), circuit depth ($2^{n-1}$), and the number of free parameters required for the unitary.
important_parameters: The native operation is the bitstring-conditioned rotation $C^{(n-1)}R(	heta, \phi)$. The fidelity measurements are performed on Haar-random unitaries.
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes that rotations conditioned on distinct control-register eigenstates can be executed in parallel with independently tunable amplitudes and phases.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the minimal-depth circuit synthesis based on CSD. Other figures detail the decomposition into $\pi/2$ rotations and the experimental setup for superconducting qubits.
paper_structure: The paper moves from theoretical protocol development (CSD-based synthesis) to establishing optimality bounds, followed by experimental implementation and fidelity measurements on superconducting hardware.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, hardware-aware roadmap for universal quantum computation, showing how specific physical constraints (native gates) can lead to provably optimal circuit decompositions, which is crucial for scaling quantum processors.
